sections.heading: Destination Snapshot
sections.body: Bohuslän is west-coast Swedish granite: crack climbing, clean faces, short approaches and enough sport routes to keep a mixed team busy. The climbing sits around the Sotenas and Stangenas peninsulas, roughly between Gothenburg and Oslo.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Destination Snapshot.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Bohuslän is one of Europe's serious granite cragging areas, but it does not feel like a heavy logistical expedition. The cliffs sit among coastline, meadows and forest, with many approaches measured in minutes rather than hours.

The main draw is traditional granite climbing: cracks, faces, single-pitch crags and some multi-pitch outings. There is also a smaller but useful sport circuit, so the area can work for teams with different appetites for gear and bolts.

sections.heading: History And Reputation
sections.body: Bohuslän has a strong reputation for granite crack and face climbing, with routes spanning from moderate traditional grades to hard test pieces. It is a destination for climbers who care about movement quality and rock rather than roadside volume alone.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for History And Reputation.

sections.heading: Rock And Climbing Character
sections.body:
Expect high-quality granite with cracks, faces and slabs. The area is known mainly for trad climbing, but the current guidebook coverage also includes fully bolted sport routes.

Most crags are compact outcrops rather than huge alpine walls, which makes the climbing day efficient. The granite style rewards footwork, jamming, gear judgement and a calm head above protection.

sections.heading: Who It Suits
sections.body: Bohuslän suits trad climbers who want varied granite days without committing to big-mountain logistics. It can also work for mixed groups because the sport routes add a bolted option, and the short approaches make family trips more realistic than many trad destinations.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Who It Suits.

sections.heading: Grades And Scale
sections.body:
The current guidebook coverage lists more than 1,800 climbs, with roughly 1,500 trad routes and 300 fully bolted sport routes. The range runs from Severe to E9, so the area is not just a hard-climber venue.

The guidebook covers 91 crags, with most within about 30 minutes by car from Brodalen or Bovallstrand.

sections.heading: Season
sections.body: The practical climbing season runs from April to October. Summer gives the easiest travel conditions, while spring and autumn can be excellent when the granite is dry and the temperatures are cooler.

sections.heading: Getting There
sections.body: Bohuslän sits roughly halfway between Gothenburg and Oslo. Flying into either city and hiring a car is the cleanest plan, because the climbing is spread across many crags on the coast and nearby peninsulas.

sections.heading: Local Tips And Rules
sections.body: Use the crag selector and maps before driving out; the value here is choosing the right granite venue for the weather, grade and team. Many crags are close to the road, but navigation still matters because the area is spread out.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Treat this as a trad granite destination first. Bring the gear and judgement for cracks and faces, and do not let the short approaches make the routes feel more casual than they are.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Bohuslän mostly trad climbing? Yes. The area is mainly known for granite trad climbing, with a smaller sport-climbing circuit.

Do you need a car? For a normal climbing trip, yes. The crags are spread out across the coast and peninsulas.

Is it only for hard climbers? No. The documented grade range is broad, from moderate trad grades to E9.
